references.title: Comparative Evaluation of Carboxyhemoglobin Quantification in Postmortem Whole Blood by CO-Oximetry and Headspace Gas Chromatography with Flame Ionization Detection and Atom Absorption Spectrophotometry
references.note: Abstract-level verification only; full text not read.
references.used_for: Method comparison of multiwavelength CO-oximetry and headspace GC-FID (CO reduced to methane) with iron by AAS in postmortem whole blood; Bland-Altman agreement over the measured range, individual deviating and one false-negative sample, between-assay bias and precision, satisfactory proficiency-test performance.

references.title: Analysis of carbon monoxide
references.note: Review; abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Exposure assessed as blood carboxyhaemoglobin saturation; simple spectrophotometric methods based on differential protein precipitation or dithionite reduction are prone to interference from other haemoglobin pigments and imprecise at low levels; automated CO-oximeters recommended for most clinical purposes; GC methods needed for low-level exposure and for postmortem blood altered by putrefaction or heat stress.

references.title: An accurate method for the determination of carboxyhemoglobin in postmortem blood using GC-TCD
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Confirmation of a spectrophotometric result by a second technique based on a different analytical principle; methaemoglobin does not bind CO, so loss of CO-binding capacity biases GC methods that compute %COHb from the ratio of unsaturated to CO-saturated blood; adding sodium dithionite reduces methaemoglobin and removes the error.

references.title: Determination of carboxyhemoglobin in the presence of other blood hemoglobin pigments by visible spectrophotometry
references.note: Abstract-level verification only; no DOI in PubMed record.
references.used_for: Postmortem blood spectrophotometry biased by pigments other than oxy-, carboxy- and reduced haemoglobin (notably methaemoglobin and sulfhaemoglobin); absorbance-difference measurement at isosbestic points with a methaemoglobin correction; qualitative confirmation by spectral detail, dithionite reduction and first-derivative spectra; accuracy diminished in denatured/autolysed blood while identification remains reliable.

references.title: Stability of blood carbon monoxide and hemoglobins during heating
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Heated blood shows deteriorated absorbance spectra and double-wavelength spectrophotometry gives wrong %COHb; a fire-casualty sample gave a significantly higher spectrophotometric %COHb than headspace GC with thermal conductivity detection; different heat susceptibility and precipitability of haemoglobin forms causes artificial increase of %COHb; spontaneous CO produced during heating.

references.title: Automated determination of carboxyhemoglobin contents in autopsy materials using head-space gas chromatography/mass spectrometry
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Automated headspace GC/MS for routine COHb in autopsy material including thermocoagulated, putrefied and contaminated specimens; CO released with potassium ferricyanide, internal standard, parallel CO-saturated aliquot for total haemoglobin; practical for blood and bone-marrow aspirates, confirming CO-oximeter findings.

references.title: An accurate method for microanalysis of carbon monoxide in putrid postmortem blood by head-space gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS/GC/MS)
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Headspace GC/MS on a molecular-sieve column for COHb in putrid postmortem blood: linear relationship between CO peak area and COHb%, small sample volumes, good reproducibility; stated advantages over UV spectrometry.

references.title: Microanalysis of carbon monoxide in blood by head-space capillary gas chromatography
references.note: Abstract-level verification only; no DOI in PubMed record.
references.used_for: Headspace capillary GC with a micro thermal conductivity detector for carboxyhaemoglobin: sensitivity and resolution, short analysis time, gradual and reproducible CO release when sulphuric acid is used as liberating agent.

references.title: Estimation of perimortal percent carboxy-heme in nonstandard postmortem specimens using analysis of carbon monoxide by GC/MS and iron by flame atomic absorption spectrophotometry
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: When normal blood is unavailable (decomposed, formalin-fixed, embalmed, exhumed, fire-dried specimens) usual COHb methods frequently fail; acid liberation of CO into a headspace vial with GC/MS quantitation by standard addition plus iron by flame AAS in the same aliquot, carboxy-heme saturation calculated from the CO/Fe ratio; tissues included spleen, liver, muscle, dried blood.

references.title: Carbon monoxide stability in stored postmortem blood samples
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Carboxyhaemoglobin found stable in postmortem blood collected in vacutainer tubes with or without preservative and stored refrigerated for up to two years, measured with CO-oximeters at autopsy and after storage.

references.title: New strategy for carbon monoxide poisoning diagnosis: Carboxyhemoglobin (COHb) vs Total Blood Carbon Monoxide (TBCO)
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Blood samples are susceptible to alteration of the optical state and to degradation during sampling, transport and storage, which strongly affects spectrophotometric analysis; over one month of storage COHb changed significantly while chromatographically measured total blood CO stayed relatively stable irrespective of temperature, time and tube headspace volume; storage parameters studied included temperature, preservative, time, headspace volume, initial saturation and freeze-thaw/reopening cycles.

references.title: A new approach for the carbon monoxide (CO) exposure diagnosis: measurement of total CO in human blood versus carboxyhemoglobin (HbCO)
references.note: Abstract-level verification only; the cut-off values proposed by the authors are deliberately not reproduced in the card.
references.used_for: In postmortem cases HbCO measured by spectrophotometry frequently gives inaccurate results because of inadequate samples or analyses, so the role of CO can be misclassified; headspace GC-MS measures total CO (bound plus dissociated), from which HbCO can be estimated.

references.title: Confirmation of the pulse oximetry gap in carbon monoxide poisoning
references.note: Abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: Finger-probe pulse oximetry readings stayed high across the range of carboxyhaemoglobin saturations and failed to detect the decrease in measured oxyhaemoglobin saturation; pulse oximetry must be considered unreliable until carboxyhaemoglobin has been measured by direct spectrophotometric determination.

references.title: Livor Mortis and Forensic Dermatology: A Review of Death-Related Gravity-Dependent Lividity and Postmortem Hypostasis
references.note: Narrative review; abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: The colour of lividity may suggest a cause of death, but cherry-red or pink lividity is associated with carbon monoxide intoxication, hypothermia or cyanide poisoning alike, i.e. it is not specific.

references.title: Interprétation des valeurs du CO expiré en tabacologie
references.note: Article in French (PubMed shows the translated title '[Interpretation of exhaled CO levels in studies on smoking]'); abstract-level verification only.
references.used_for: CO is a non-specific biomarker of tobacco exposure with a short half-life; exhaled CO reflects the intensity of smoke inhalation and correlates strongly and linearly with blood carboxyhaemoglobin; elimination varies with sex, ventilation, exercise and time of day; several non-smoking conditions raise CO, so false positives and increased endogenous CO production must be taken into account when interpreting COHb.

references.title: Carboxyhemoglobin half-life toxicokinetic profiles during and after normobaric oxygen therapy: On a swine model
references.note: Experimental swine model; abstract-level verification only. Cited only for the fact that oxygen administration governs COHb decline over time.
references.used_for: Carboxyhaemoglobin declines under normobaric oxygen administration following a bi-compartmental rather than mono-compartmental model, and a slight rebound was observed after oxygen was stopped; extravascular CO storage cannot be estimated in routine practice.
